args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Follow-up needed: root-cause v2.3.1 and review why it was promoted despite unhealthy staging rc.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001**, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** The latest deploy put v2.3.1 in production in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also failed health checks in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions now run v2.3.0, the service passes health checks, and the error rate is about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The summary covers the failure, the rollback and the current healthy state. It also flags follow-ups: finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and finding out why v2.3.1 was released even though its candidate failed in staging.

No approval was needed, because the rule requiring one only covers versions that have never been healthy in production.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
